land.text: the Vidin lands: in 1356 Ivan Alexander 'isolated Vidin from the Bulgarian monarchy' for his son Ivan Sratsimir

predecessors.note: Cliopatria draws the Vidin shape from 1363; the Bulgarian dossier (eu-18-c) records the 1356 split.

land.text: Vidin and its lands: after the defeat at Nicopolis 'Vidin fell under Ottoman control' by the end of 1396 or the beginning of 1397

successors.note: Some historians hold that Constantine II ruled Vidin as an Ottoman vassal from 1397 (Tsardom of Vidin page); Cliopatria keeps the state to 1401.

rulers.name: Ivan Sratsimir
rulers.title: Tsar of Vidin
rulers.note: Proclaimed in Vidin in 1356; held by Louis I of Hungary 1365-1369 and restored in autumn 1369; captured by the Ottomans at the end of 1396 or early 1397 and imprisoned at Bursa. His son Constantine II claimed the title (the Tsardom of Vidin page: Constantine II 1396-1422 or 1397-1422, disputed).

correction.text: the 1363 shape (Vidin on the Danube) extended back to 1356, when Sratsimir 'was proclaimed emperor in Vidin'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria begins in 1363, the pages put Sratsimir's rule at Vidin from 1356. Neither gives a boundary; the 1363 outline is the nearest drawn extent (confidence 2).

17,072 km2 on the Danube from the Timok to the Iskar/Ogosta area. Neither page gives an area. The Hungarian occupation 1365-1369 does not change the outline; the ledger carries it as an occupation (hatched). 'Vidin was the only region controlled by the indigenous Bulgarian population' after 1393.

16,384 km2: one cell gained on the Danube and three lost in the south against 1363; no page opened gives districts (the Ivan Sratsimir page and the Tsardom of Vidin page mention no Timok, Morava or Sofia lands), so this is unverified: page budget.

correction.text: unchanged shape, valid for 1395-1396 only; the Ottomans hold Vidin from the end of 1396 or early 1397 ('seized it by the end of 1396 or the beginning of 1397')

keyframe_review.note: Years only: Cliopatria draws the state to 1401. The pages end the state in 1396 (infobox 'disestablished 1396'); for 1397-1401 the land is Ottoman, ruled at most by Constantine II as a vassal, which the Ottoman dossier should draw (vassal tint) if the reviewer accepts that reading. region.text: Vidin and its lands on the Danube

ledger.note: 1356: Ivan Sratsimir is proclaimed emperor at Vidin. 'Ivan Sratsimir was proclaimed emperor in Vidin in 1356'; the Tsardom page: Ivan Alexander 'isolated Vidin from the Bulgarian monarchy' that year (its infobox says 'Established: 1369', the year of the restoration after the Hungarian occupation).

region.text: the Vidin Tsardom, conquered between June and September 1365

ledger.note: June 1365: Louis I of Hungary takes Vidin. 'Louis I marched from Hungary on 1 May 1365 and captured Vidin on 2 June after a brief siege'; 'The rest of the Vidin Tsardom was conquered in the next three months.'

Autumn 1369: Louis I restores Ivan Sratsimir. 'Louis I had to give up his claims and restore Ivan Sratsimir to the throne in Vidin in the autumn of 1369', after an Orthodox coalition of Vladislav I Vlaicu of Wallachia and Dobrotitsa; the page gives no month.

region.text: the Tsardom of Vidin, the last Bulgarian state after Tarnovo fell in 1393

ledger.note: 1396: Vidin falls to Bayezid after Nicopolis. Sratsimir's troops joined the Christian army that 'suffered a heavy defeat on 25 September in the battle of Nicopolis'; the sultan 'seized it by the end of 1396 or the beginning of 1397' and Sratsimir was imprisoned at Bursa. Tsardom page: 'After the defeat ... Vidin fell under Ottoman control'; infobox 'disestablished 1396'.

wars.name: Hungarian conquest of Vidin (Louis I)
wars.outcome: Louis I took Vidin on 2 June 1365 and the rest of the Tsardom within three months; he had to restore Ivan Sratsimir in autumn 1369 after a coalition of Vladislav I Vlaicu and Dobrotitsa.
wars.note: The Tsardom page says only that the occupation 'was short-lived'; neither page mentions a 'Banat of Bulgaria'.

wars.name: Crusade of Nicopolis
wars.outcome: Christian defeat at Nicopolis on 25 September 1396; Vidin seized by Bayezid by the end of 1396 or early 1397; Ivan Sratsimir imprisoned at Bursa.
wars.note: Sratsimir contributed soldiers to the crusade (the Tsardom of Vidin page).

certainty.note: Neither page gives districts or a boundary; the Danube front and the Ottoman and Hungarian frontiers are approximate.

sources.title: Tsardom of Vidin
sources.note: Infobox (dates 1369-1396 as the page prints them), founding 1356, Hungarian occupation 1365-1369, Ottoman fall 1396, Constantine II.

sources.title: Ivan Sratsimir of Bulgaria
sources.note: Dated reign: 1356 proclamation, 1 May / 2 June 1365 Hungarian campaign, autumn 1369 restoration, 1388 Ottoman vassalage, 25 September 1396 Nicopolis, end of 1396 / early 1397 loss.

notes: Pages: Tsardom of Vidin and Ivan Sratsimir of Bulgaria (budget 1-2). Settled: start 1356; end 1396 (the Tsardom page's 'disestablished 1396'; Ivan Sratsimir page: lost by the end of 1396 or early 1397). Cliopatria draws the state to 1401: the 1397-1401 years are Ottoman land (Constantine II claimed the title, some historians say as a vassal, 1397-1422) and need an Ottoman vassal event if the reviewer accepts that reading; the pages do not give the extent. Not recorded in this ledger because they belong to the suzerain's dossier: Ottoman vassalage from 1388 (the Ivan Sratsimir page: 'had to become an Ottoman vassal and to accept an Ottoman garrison in Vidin'; the page does not date a 1371 submission); the ottoman-empire dossier (me-10) should carry vassal_start 1388 and vassal_end 1396 with counterpart despotate-of-vidin. Pages silent on: the Timok/Morava/Sofia lands, the 1375 cell changes, a 'Banat of Bulgaria', Wallachian relations beyond the 1369 alliance. The Tsardom page's infobox 'Established 1369' is the restoration, not the founding.
